title: AI assistant for freight brokers on Mac: a voice helper for Gmail, Excel and Sheets
metaTitle: AI Assistant for Freight Brokers on Mac | Lazur
description: Lazur is a voice assistant for freight brokers on Mac. Ask about carrier emails, invoices and spreadsheets, and it points at what to do next.
intro: Lazur is an AI assistant for freight brokers on your Mac. It sees your screen while you hold a key, answers out loud, and points at the cell, email or button you need. It works in any app, but it never clicks for you, so your TMS, Gmail and sheets stay under your control.
tldr: Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and it answers out loud.
It explains, points and guides. It does not click buttons, send emails or book loads for you.
Good uses for brokers: carrier email questions, sheet formulas, call notes by dictation, and carrier lookups as background research.
Your employer decides what carrier and driver data can go into any AI tool. Check that rule before a live load.
Lazur runs on macOS with Apple silicon or Intel. Windows is planned, not available.

blocks.text: What an AI assistant for freight brokers does on your Mac

An AI assistant for freight brokers has one job on your Mac. It answers the question in front of you, inside the app you already have open. Lazur does that with your voice. Hold ⌥⌘, which means Option and Command together, and ask. Lazur looks at your screen during that moment, answers out loud, and can point at the spot you mean.

It does three kinds of work. It explains what you see, such as a rate column that does not add up. It points, drawing a circle and a label around the cell, button or message you asked about. It guides, walking you through a menu or setting one click at a time while it waits for each click. It does not do the clicking for you, and it does not operate your TMS.

Some features matter more if you write all day. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Lazur also runs research in its own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report. That covers the lookups you do between calls.
Where a freight broker's day goes, according to the research

No independent study measures a freight broker's day from start to finish. The best numbers come from Microsoft's office studies and from freight vendors. Microsoft's data covers knowledge workers in general. Vendors publish their own estimates. Each figure below names who measured it, so you can judge how far to trust it.

In Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index, email took 15% of the average employee's Microsoft 365 time. Teams meetings took 23%, and Teams chat took 19%. Content creation took 43%, and Excel alone took 18%. The data covers a rolling 28-day window and excludes weekends. No public study measures how much of that is spreadsheet time for brokers.

Microsoft's June 2025 study adds volume. The average knowledge worker gets 117 emails and 153 Teams messages a day. 40% check email before 6 a.m., and 29% of active workers are back in their inbox by 10 p.m. Brokers add carrier and shipper threads on top of those numbers.

blocks.text: AI tools for carrier emails, phone calls and invoices

Carrier work is where many brokers lose the rest of the day. FreightCaviar's poll says brokers settle invoice disputes with carriers mainly by email (47%) or by phone (46%). The company ran that poll itself and does not state a sample size, so treat it as a signal.

FreightWaves reported in December 2025 on research from OTR Solutions. About 68% of surveyed brokerages experienced financial stress over the past year. In accounts payable, 54% say the work is mostly automated, but only 2% have achieved full automation. For accounts receivable, 43% say it is only partly automated, with many manual steps left.

LaneSurf, a freight software vendor, says a rep may spend 4+ hours a day on outbound carrier communication across email, phone and text. It also says carrier sales reps typically run 50 to 150 outbound carrier contacts a day. It attributes both to its operational data and names no study, so test them against your own week.

blocks.title: Measure your own week
blocks.text: Keep a tally for one full week. Write down minutes in email, on the phone, and in each spreadsheet. Vendor numbers only help if your week looks like theirs.
How to use Lazur's ⌥⌘ shortcut on carrier emails and sheets

Hold ⌥⌘ and keep holding while you talk. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while the keys are down. Let go, and it stops. Audio and a screenshot go to AI providers to answer. They are not stored.

Ask in plain words. Say 'What does this carrier want before it releases the BOL?' Lazur reads the thread on screen and answers out loud. If you ask 'Where is the detention line?' it draws a circle and a label so you can find the cell fast.

Put the right thing on screen first. Lazur sees what is visible at that moment. If the email you mean is scrolled off, scroll to it, then hold the keys. A wrong answer usually traces back to the wrong part of the screen.
Guide mode for steps you do not know yet

Some broker tasks are menu work. Think of exporting a sheet as a PDF, sorting a load list by pickup date, or setting up a Gmail label. Ask Lazur to walk you through it. It guides one click at a time and waits for each click before it names the next step.

Do not ask it to just do the task. It will not click for you. Ask for the path, keep your hand on the mouse, and follow it. The first run takes longer. The second run is faster, and you learn where the menu lives. For sorting, see [sort data by column in Google Sheets](/how-to/sort-data-by-column-in-google-sheets).
Dictate carrier notes with fn
Hold fn to dictate. Lazur turns your speech into clean text at the cursor, in any app. For a broker that means call notes, dispute emails and load comments, typed while your eyes stay on the carrier.

A few features save the most repeat work. Snippets hold text you send often, such as a standard dispute reply opener. The personal dictionary keeps the words Lazur gets wrong, like carrier names and terms such as MC and BOL. Clipboard slots hold a value you need in another app, such as a BOL number, while you switch windows.

items: Add each regular carrier name to the personal dictionary once. Misspellings stop repeating in your notes.
Save your carrier packet request as a snippet. Insert it with one dictation instead of retyping it.
Put the load number in a clipboard slot before you switch to your TMS, so you can paste it back in one step.

blocks.title: Read before you send
blocks.text: Dictated text lands wherever the cursor sits. Check the recipient, the load number and the amount before you send anything to a carrier.
Excel and Google Sheets for margins, invoices and lookups

Brokers live in sheets. Load lists, rate sheets, margin checks and invoice matches all sit in Excel or Google Sheets. Lazur helps in Excel for Mac, and in Google Sheets in Chrome. It reads the formula or the error on screen, then explains it out loud. For the Excel side, see [Excel for freight brokers on Mac](/for/freight-brokers/excel).

Start with a question, not a formula. Ask 'Why is this cell showing N/A?' or 'What does this formula add up?' Lazur names the function and points at the cells it depends on. You type the fix yourself. That keeps the sheet in your hands and teaches you the formula.

Check these first when a sheet looks wrong. A lookup that returns N/A often has a stray space, or a number stored as text. A total that comes up short often includes text numbers. Filters can also hide rows you expected to count, so clear them before you trust a sum.

Email triage in Gmail and Outlook for Mac

Gmail on a Mac runs in Safari or Chrome, and Lazur works in either. Use Gmail's own tools for timing. Snooze a thread until a carrier calls back, or schedule a reply for the morning. See [how to snooze an email in Gmail](/how-to/snooze-an-email-in-gmail) and [how to schedule an email in Gmail](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail).
Ask Lazur for the first run. Say 'How do I snooze this thread?' It guides one click at a time. After a few runs, the shortcut is faster than the guide.
Outlook for Mac: check which version you run

Microsoft's support page describes new Outlook for Mac, which you switch on or off with a Legacy Outlook setting. It says support for legacy Outlook for Mac will end in October 2026. Continued support depends on your Microsoft 365, Office or Outlook license. If you are still on legacy, ask IT what your company plans.

To check, look in the Help menu. If you see Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook, you run the new version. Microsoft's release notes list 16.114.3 as the latest Outlook for Mac build, dated October 27, 2026. Open Outlook > About Outlook and compare your build number.

blocks.title: Do not assume it is current
blocks.text: Your company may pin an older build or a different license. Confirm the build with IT before you build a workflow around one feature.
Look up a carrier without leaving your sheet

Carrier vetting is a list of lookups. You check authority, insurance, safety record and whether the legal name matches the MC number. Lazur can run those checks as a background job. It works in its own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension, then returns a summary and a report.

Keep the request short and exact. For example: 'Check authority and insurance on file for these MC numbers, and list any mismatch with the legal name.' A long list gives a long report, and a long report is slower to check. Start with the carriers you are about to book.

Verify the result on the official carrier record before you book. A summary is a starting point, not paperwork. Lazur's research does not replace the carrier packet or the insurance certificate, so keep both in your file.
Privacy, carrier data and your company's rules

Freight files hold personal data. Driver names, phone numbers, payment details and shipper contacts appear on screen all day. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

That does not decide whether your company allows it. Your employer sets the rules for customer, carrier and driver data, and they apply to any AI tool. Ask your IT or compliance contact before you use Lazur on live loads. This page describes how Lazur handles data. It is not a compliance certification, and it does not replace your company's obligations.

blocks.title: Before a live load
blocks.text: Close windows that show bank details or personal identifiers before you hold the keys. Lazur can only see what is on screen at that moment.
What Lazur does not do for freight brokers

Setting expectations saves frustration. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app. It has no partnership with any app maker, and it has no integration with any TMS maker.

items: It does not book loads, send emails or update a rate sheet for you.
It does not replace your rate confirmation, bill of lading or proof of delivery.
It runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.
DAT's Broker TMS page describes invoices and BOLs sent in a few clicks, but it does not mention Mac or a browser-only option. Confirm your TMS runs on your machine.

blocks.text: Mistakes brokers make with an AI assistant

items: Asking a vague question. Name the app and the cell, or the email, first.
Trusting a lookup summary without checking the official carrier record.
Dictating a dispute note and sending it unread.
Leaving an unchecked Outlook version in place when IT has a different plan.
Pasting a whole carrier packet on screen when one question would do.

blocks.text: Each mistake costs time, and some cost money. The fix is small. Narrow the question, check the source, and read the text before it leaves your hands.
How to start using Lazur for freight brokerage work

items: Download Lazur from the [download page](/download) and open it on your Mac.
Start the Pro trial. It needs no credit card and begins the first time you open the app.
Hold ⌥⌘ over a carrier email and ask one question you already know the answer to. Check the reply.
Dictate your next call note with fn, and add your regular carriers to the personal dictionary.
Ask for one guided path, such as a Gmail label, so you learn that menu once.

faq.question: Is Lazur built only for freight brokers?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that works across apps. This page shows how a freight broker might use it on carrier email, sheets and lookups. It has no freight-only version and no integration with a TMS maker.

faq.question: Can Lazur work inside my TMS?
faq.answer: It can see your screen in any Mac app, so it can explain a TMS page that is open on your Mac. It does not operate the TMS. DAT's page does not mention Mac, so confirm with your TMS vendor that it runs on your machine.

faq.question: Will Lazur send emails or book loads for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts text and dictates it at your cursor. You read it and send it yourself. It does not click buttons or operate other apps.

faq.question: Is carrier and driver data safe to use with Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Your employer decides whether that fits its rules, so check first. This is not a compliance certification.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Which Outlook should a broker use on Mac?
faq.answer: Check your version first. Microsoft says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026, and continued support depends on your license. Ask IT which version your company supports.

faq.question: How much does Lazur cost for a broker?
faq.answer: Lazur has a Pro trial and a Power plan. Check the pricing page for current prices, since they may change.

faq.question: Are the freight statistics on this page reliable?
faq.answer: Treat them as signals. The Microsoft figures cover knowledge workers in general. The FreightCaviar, Keelway and LaneSurf figures come from vendors, and their methods are not fully stated. Measure your own week for one full week.

faq.question: Can Lazur check a carrier's authority and insurance?
faq.answer: It can run those lookups as background research in its own Chrome tabs, then return a summary and a report. Verify the carrier record yourself before you book.
